title: Hal Higdon Novice 5K Training Program (8 weeks)
population: Beginning runners, or runners wanting a low-mileage approach
findings: 8-week plan with 3 run days (Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday), run/walk or rest on Monday and Wednesday, Friday rest, and Sunday a timed walk; the longest run is 3 miles (4.8 km).
Tuesday and Saturday runs build from 1.5 mi in week 1 to 3 mi in week 7 in 0.25 mi steps; the Thursday run is 1.5-2 mi.
Sunday is a timed walk rising from 30 min in week 1 to 60 min in week 7; the 5K race is in week 8.
limitations: Read through a page-fetch summariser. Convention, not evidence. Year is the access date.
implications: Couch-to-5K style start: the longest run for a new runner is 3 miles (about 30-35 min, estimate) after 8 weeks, with the weekend session mainly a timed walk.
Engine inference: a new runner's longest run can grow by about 0.25 mi per week across three run days instead of being a share target.
